Thank you to everyone who replied, argued, shared and showed us their work this month.

You're the culture we keep talking about.
Studio habit worth stealing: before presenting anything, explain it to someone outside the project in one sentence. If they don't get it, neither will the client.
Name a shop in Slemani whose sign you could draw from memory. That's what a strong brand looks like.
A sketch goes in the bin once we've decided it isn't the one. Keeping the bin means nobody spends next week arguing for an idea we already tested and dropped.
Be honest: how many files on your desktop are called final-final? No judgement here.

Trends travel fast now. A look that starts somewhere else arrives here within a week.

The brands that last aren't the fastest to copy. They're the ones worth copying.
Every brand has a voice, whether it chose one or not. The ones that chose sound like a person; the rest sound like a form.
Autumn in Slemani: the first cold morning, school bags everywhere, and someone's grandmother insisting you take a jacket.
If you're a designer in Kurdistan who has never shown your work online, post one piece this week and tag us. We'll be your first comment.

Studio note: the best feedback this week came from someone who isn't a designer.

They didn't know the rules. They knew what they felt. Listen to those people.

To every student in Slemani with a sketchbook open at 3am and a deadline at 9: the habit of caring this much about one curve or one colour is exactly what clients end up paying for. Get some sleep when you can.
Arabic-script logos often get squeezed into a box that was drawn for English. Give them their own space and the curves start to make sense.
Good design in Kurdistan doesn't need permission from Dubai, London or anywhere else.
When a brief says “modern,” ask what that means. The answer is usually the real brief.

Which Kurdish word is the most beautiful to look at, not just to say?

We're asking for a reason.
Which brand from Kurdistan would you wear on a T-shirt, unpaid, just because you like it?
Copying a competitor's look is the most expensive way to stay in second place.

Ask any AI tool for a logo and you'll get something competent in seconds. So will your competitor. Competent is about to cost nothing; what still costs money is the decision that makes a brand recognisable, like the colour nobody else would pick or the line only you would say.

That's the work we do. 33studio.org
Respect to the sign painters, tailors, bakers and calligraphers of this city. They were doing branding long before anyone called it that.
Taste isn't what you like. It's what you're willing to say no to.

Ask a kid in Slemani to write their name and they'll switch between two alphabets without thinking about it.

Our brands should be that fluent.
Most logos fail at the size they're used most: tiny, on a phone, next to forty other logos. Design for that size first.

The best wayfinding system in this city is still “turn left at the old bakery.”

Every brand should be that easy to remember.

Right-to-left isn't a problem to solve. It's a rhythm to design with.

The page reads differently. So should the design.
How we start a logo, in four steps. A short thread.
Open Desk: show us the first thing you ever designed. Be honest; the worse it is, the better.
A brand guide that nobody opens is a very expensive PDF.

Before anyone rented desks by the month, Slemani had tea houses: one small table, two strangers, and a glass that never stayed empty for long. Plenty of good ideas in this city were first argued over tea.

Which tea house is yours?

Open Desk: who's the most underrated creative in Kurdistan right now? Illustrator, photographer, calligrapher, anyone.

Name them below and tell us why. We'll start following.
Kurdish has letters an English designer never has to draw, like ڕ and ڵ. For anyone who loves type, that's extra material to play with.
Print your logo the size of a coin and pin it to a wall for a day. If you can still read it from across the room by the evening, it's ready for a shop sign.

Slemani wakes up in a particular order: bread ovens, tea, traffic, and then the first argument about football.

What's the first sound of your morning?

Hand-painted shop signs from Slemani, collected one street at a time.

#sulaimanyah #33studio #designinspiration #designagency #creativeagency

Kurdish is one of the most beautiful scripts to design with, and one of the least designed for.

We intend to change that, one letter at a time.

Studio note: we killed our favourite idea today. It was clever. It just wasn't true.

That's the job.

The best palettes are found, not chosen. Walk through any bazaar in Slemani and you'll see more colour sense than in most brand guidelines.

What colour is your city?

Your product is excellent. Your Instagram says otherwise.

Let's fix the part customers see first. 33studio.org

Your brand is judged in this order: how it looks, how it sounds, how it behaves.

Most businesses only work on the third. We help with all three. 33studio.org

We’re proud to see our brand identity and system for TOROS now live on Ads of the World.

Most brands in the power-accessories category compete on the same promise: more capacity, more charge, and more numbers on the box.

We wanted TOROS to move differently!

The identity was built around one central thought: power only matters when it moves

That idea shaped the entire system from the forward-leaning wordmark and charged visual language to the product architecture connecting batteries, powerbanks, chargers, and cables under one recognisable behaviour

Different products. One current.

Brand identity and system by 33Studio

#BrandIdentity #BrandStrategy #PackagingDesign #AdsOfTheWorld #33Studio

Every brand in the category talks about more
More capacity
More charge
More numbers on the box…

TOROS starts somewhere else…
We believe power only matters when it moves
A battery sitting still is just potential. A charger in a drawer is just an object. But put power in motion and it becomes something useful a day extended, a journey continued, a connection kept alive.

That became the idea behind TOROS.

Rather than building a collection of disconnected accessories, we created one unified brand system where every product carries the same sense of movement, energy, and forward momentum.

Powerbanks. Chargers. AUX cables. Batteries.
Different products. One current.

The identity is built around a simple belief: energy has no reason to stand still.

Every element of the system — from the visual language to the product architecture is designed to feel active, direct, and always moving forward.

Because TOROS isn’t about how much power you have.
It’s about what you do with it.

TOROS,
Motion is Energy.

Brand identity & system for TOROS, by @33studio.iq 

#33studio #toros #battery #auxulry
